body: Quick pass: merges cleanly with main, author's quick gate green on 9c14570a (pins in `crates/app/tests/stock_source_verdict.rs`), body complete. Flagged ready; a gouge check, so it gets the high-tier review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 9c14570a41fe1d73092db0eb42d05e87cba64011 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** Clause 3 ("some op names a separate non-fixture part") can be met by a model that is not the part being cut. When that happens, the real finished part leaves the verdict and a 5 mm gouge into it posts.

### What I built, ran and tried
Worktree on `9c14570a`, trial-merged with current `origin/main` (already up to date, no conflicts), debug build.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `stock_source_verdict` | 6 passed |
| `edge_break_gate` | 5 passed |
| `solid_law_goldens` | 1 passed |
| `stock_sim_document` | 9 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| `operations` | 117 passed, 6 ignored |
| lib `stock_sim` / `setup_align` | 7 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I also wrote throwaway probe tests locally. They were removed afterwards and never committed or pushed.

### Requested before merge
1. **A real gouge into the true part posts when the stock is made from that part and any op names another model** (`crates/app/src/stock_source.rs:72-77`, clause 3).
   Reproduction, using the fixtures from `stock_source_verdict.rs`:
   - import `part()` as "part", and a separate block "other" at X 80..100;
   - `SetStock FromModel { source: "part" }`;
   - Op1 = `bore(FLOOR - 5.0)` on `SrcRef::Stock`, generated;
   - Op2 = `bore(FLOOR)` on `SrcRef::Entity("other")`.

   Results:
   - `stock_only_model` returns `Some("part")`.
   - `verification_gate` returns `[]`.
   - `posting::post_setup` returns `Ok(())`.
   - Without "other", the same job refuses: `post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 812 cell(s), worst 5.00 mm`. That is today's verdict, and the one this PR's own `without_a_separate_part_the_casting_keeps_todays_verdict` promises to keep.

   Why it matters: a stock made from the finished part is a real workflow. It is how `edge_break_gate` does deburr, chamfer and engrave on a finished part. Any second model touched by any op breaks the guarantee that the decision file's "Stock made from the part itself" bullet relies on, for example a second part on the table, an engraving or text model, or a soft jaw or reference body that is not flagged as a fixture.
2. **A suppressed op is enough to drop the part** (`stock_source.rs:66`). `named` collects the sources of every op, suppressed ones included. Counting suppressed ops is right for clause 2, because it keeps more geometry judged. For clause 3 it is the dangerous direction: an op that is not even in the program "provides" the separate part. Same reproduction as item 1, but Op2 is suppressed (`EditOperationParams::with_suppressed`) and never generated. The result is the same: the 5 mm gouge posts with an empty gate.
3. **Clause 2 does not see area picks.** `named_by` (`stock_source.rs:18-24`) reads only `op.src`. An op on `SrcRef::Stock` whose boundary is picked on the casting/part (`AreaControls` → `ExtraBoundary { shape: BoundaryShape::Picks(..) }`, `OpenBoundary.picks`, `crates/app/src/operation/types/area.rs:50,76`) names that model, but it does not count as naming it. That op is exactly "machining the part on the stock", and the model still drops out. This is not reproduced separately; it follows from item 1 plus reading the code.

Possible fixes (the author's choice; any one that makes items 1 to 3 hold is fine):
- Clause 3 counts only unsuppressed ops.
- Clause 3 also requires the separate part to sit inside the stock source's envelope. A casting contains its part; an unrelated model beside the finished part does not.
- Clause 2 also reads `area` picks, and any other `GeoSel` an op carries.

Please pin it with the reproduction above as a test that must refuse, in both the plain and the suppressed variant. The decision file's fallback, an explicit "stock source only" mark, also closes all three.

### Attacks that held
- **Source kinds.** `SrcRef::Stock` names nothing. `Entity` and every `Selection` `GeoSel.entity` count for clause 2. Hole data in Bore/Drill params is literal coordinates (no model name). A fixture never meets clause 3.
- **Several setups.** A flip setup whose stock is a different shape, or a box stock, fails clause 1, so the casting stays judged. A setup whose stock entity is missing returns `None` (judged).
- **Post entry points.** `verification_report` runs live on every post. I found no cached verdict, so adding an op on the casting after the fact is seen at once. Undo/redo of `SetStock` and of `CreateOperation` is pinned by the PR's tests.
- **Identity.** The rule compares by name. `update_model` propagates a re-imported model into its `FromModel` stock (M3.1 B), so stock and source stay the same geometry.
- **Other readers.** `part_facets_as_modelled` and `parts_facets_in` are read only by `stock_sim` (verdict and field view) and `stock_sim_carry::judge`. Collision, rapid and cross-drill laws read the op's own source or the stock. `model_fidelity::verdict_tol` still reads every model (false refusal at worst).
- **Code.** No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests, no indexing, provenance line present, 88 lines, tests in the owning crate, layering fine.

### Notes (not blocking)
- `stock_only_model` runs `find_by_name` (a full world walk) once per op source. That is fine at today's sizes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Reworked per the review (head b875cd66): the inferred rule is removed; the verdict leaves the stock's source out only when the user ticks "The source model is raw stock only (not judged as the part)" (default off = unchanged). The review's two reproductions are pinned as refusing tests, boundary picks count as naming the model. Details in the PR body and docs/decisions/1094-stock-source-not-part.md. Ready for a re-review; still a draft.

**Needs changes before merge.** The opt-in redesign is the right shape: both of my earlier reproductions are now pinned and refuse. One defect is left. The mark is keyed by the source model's *name*, so a new model imported under a deleted casting's name inherits it, and a real 5 mm gouge into that new model posts.

### What I built, ran and tried
Worktree on `b875cd66`, trial-merged with current `origin/main` (already up to date). I reviewed the whole diff against main, not only the change since `9c14570a`.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `stock_source_verdict` | 11 passed |
| `mcp_setup` | 7 passed |
| `edge_break_gate` | 5 passed |
| `solid_law_goldens` | 1 passed |
| `stock_sim_document` | 9 passed |
| `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| `operations` | 117 passed, 6 ignored |
| `camcraft-ui --lib raw_stock_row` | 1 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib structural` | 4 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I also wrote throwaway probe tests locally. They were removed afterwards and never committed or pushed.

### Requested before merge
1. **A new model with the old name inherits the mark, and a gouge into it posts** (`crates/app/src/stock_source.rs:70-78` `source_of`; `crates/app/src/schema.rs:114` `StockSourceOnly { source: String }`).
   Reproduction:
   - import "casting" (`casting()`) and "other" (a block at X 80..100);
   - `SetStock FromModel { source: "casting" }`, then `SetStockSourceOnly::new(true)`;
   - `DeleteEntity "casting"`;
   - `ImportModel::from_mesh("casting", part())`, i.e. the finished part, imported under the old name;
   - Op2 = `bore(FLOOR)` on `Entity("other")`; Op1 = `bore(FLOOR - 5.0)` on `SrcRef::Stock`, both generated.

   Results:
   - `stock_only_model` returns `Some("casting")`.
   - `verification_gate` returns `[]`.
   - `post_setup` returns `Ok(())`.

   `DeleteEntity` does not refuse deleting a model that a from-model stock copies, so the stock keeps both `FromModel { source: "casting" }` and the mark. Any later model wearing that name is then judged out.

   Possible fixes:
   - Clear the mark, or make it stop holding, once its source model is gone.
   - Tie the mark to the model's identity rather than its name, for example the entity, or the source model's revision/facet hash taken when the mark was set (a re-import through `update_model` could keep it on purpose).
   - Have `DeleteEntity` of a stock's source drop the mark as part of the same undo unit.

   Please pin it with the reproduction above.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **The mark revives when the stock comes back to the same source.** Mark the casting, `SetStock Box` (the mark stops holding, correct), then `SetStock FromModel(casting)` again: the mark holds again. The checkbox shows it ticked, so this is visible and the model is the same, which is acceptable. The issue is that "a different stock drops the mark" holds only while the stock is a different shape. With item 1 fixed, this is fine.
- **The refusal hint can coach hiding a real gouge.** `gouge_hint` is shown on any gouge whose program stock is from-model and whose source no op names. Take my first-round reproduction (stock made from the finished part, an op on the stock, an unrelated op on "other"). The refusal says "tick ... raw stock only", and ticking it posts the 5 mm gouge. The wording is conditional ("if ... is only the raw stock ... and the finished part is its own model"), so it is the user's informed call. A tighter trigger would show the hint only when some op names another non-fixture model whose envelope sits inside the source's.
- **A model with no facets counts as "another model to judge".** Mark the stock's source, add a model imported from an empty mesh, and op on the stock bores 5 mm into the source: `nothing_judged` stays quiet and it posts with nothing judged. The file importers most likely refuse empty meshes, so I found this only through `ImportModel::from_mesh`. `nothing_judged` could count judged facets rather than judged models.
- **Garbled project values are refused.** For `"raw_stock_only"`, the values `"true"`, `1` and `null` are each refused as `malformed project file: invalid type ...`, never read as true. A missing key reads false. An old file is judged as before.
- **Nothing sets the mark implicitly.** I checked by grep: only `SetStockSourceOnly` and the project loader write `StockSourceOnly`. A carried or copied setup stock, `DeleteEntity`/`DeleteSetup` + undo, and `CreateSetup` do not copy it, which is the safe direction: the mark is lost and you get a false refusal at worst. The MCP `set_raw_stock_only` needs an explicit `on` and has no default.
- **Source kinds that put the model back.** `SrcRef::Entity` and every `Selection` `GeoSel.entity` do, as do `area` boundary picks (`ExtraBoundary::Picks`, `OpenBoundary.picks`), suppressed ops included and ops added after the tick. `SrcRef::Stock` does not put it back, by design: facing the casting on the stock. Bore/Drill holes are literal coordinates and name no model.
- **Several setups.** Every program stock must be a marked copy of the same model, so a second setup whose from-model stock of the casting is unmarked keeps the casting judged for the whole document. One setup's mark cannot drop the model from another setup's verdict.
- **Post entry points.** `nothing_judged` sits in `posting_sim::sim_clause`, inside `verification_report`. The GUI post, `post_setup`, MCP and script all read that same gate. A remainder of fixtures only counts as nothing to judge and is refused.
- **Code.** No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests. The component is declared only in `schema.rs`. The command validates at creation (refuses with no stock, or a stock not made from a model). The UI row only queues a `CommandKind`. UI text is plain English. There is a structural test for the row and no snapshot PNG. New files are under 200 lines. `crates/ui/src/state.rs` grows a file already at 4261 lines by 17 lines (not blocking). The decision file records what was dropped, including the three-clause inference.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
